info.name: Pickaboo — vendorshop 500 diagnostics
info.description:
Isolates why GET /rest/V1/dcastalia-vendorshop/products returns 500 for shopUrl=final-shop1684744680 on staging.

Run the requests in order and read the test results in the Postman console. Each request asserts something specific; together they tell you whether the fault is the vendor's data, the Accept header, the page size, or the module itself.

Variables live on the collection — edit shopUrl / healthyShopUrl before running.

Background: the Flutter app targets staging (gcpadmin) by default; the React Native app is hardcoded to production (www). So the two apps have never hit the same backend for this endpoint, and a staging-only failure would be invisible in RN.

variable.description: REQUIRED for request 4. Any vendor whose shop page loads fine. Grab sold_by_vendor_url_key from a real product.

exec: pm.test('Reproduces the 500 seen in the app', function () {
console.log('NOT REPRODUCED — endpoint is healthy now. The app failure was transient.');

request.description:
Byte-for-byte what the Flutter app sends: no Authorization header (the app sets noAuth:true for this endpoint), Accept + Content-Type application/json.

Expected: 500, matching the app log.

exec: console.log('VERDICT: works on prod, fails on staging → staging data or staging module. Not a client bug.');
console.log('VERDICT: fails on BOTH → module-level bug. Pull the Magento exception log.');
console.log('Vendor does not exist on prod (expected — it is a staging test shop). Inconclusive; use request 4 instead.');

request.description:
Same request against the host the RN app actually uses (AppConstant.js:15 → https://www.pickaboo.com/rest).

This vendor is likely staging-only, so a 404 here is plausible and inconclusive — fall through to request 4.

item.name: 3. Staging — no Accept header (rules out content negotiation)

exec: console.log('VERDICT: the Accept header is the trigger. Flutter sets Accept: application/json globally in auth_interceptor.dart:30; RN sends only Content-Type. Scope Accept out of this call.');
console.log('Accept header is NOT the cause — same failure without it.');

request.description:
The ONE remaining difference between the two clients.

RN (AxiosService.js:7) sends only Content-Type. Flutter's AuthInterceptor adds Accept: application/json to every request. Magento does content negotiation on Accept, so this is worth eliminating before blaming the data.

Note: Postman may still send its own Accept: */* — check the actual sent headers in the console if this comes back 200.

item.name: 4. Staging — healthy vendor (is it this vendor's data?)

exec: console.warn('Set the healthyShopUrl collection variable first — any vendor whose shop page loads fine.');
console.log('VERDICT: endpoint works on staging for a good vendor → the failure is specific to ' + pm.collectionVariables.get('shopUrl') + "'s data. Nothing to fix in the app.");
console.log('VERDICT: every vendor fails on staging → module-level bug, not data. Backend needs to look at it.');

request.description:
The decisive request. If a known-good vendor returns 200 on the same host with the same headers, the module is fine and final-shop1684744680's catalog data is the problem.

Set healthyShopUrl first — take sold_by_vendor_url_key off any real product's detail response.

item.name: 5. Staging — pageSize 20 (the value Flutter used to send)

exec: console.log('Compare against request 1 (pageSize=10). Different codes would mean page size matters — unlikely, but it was the only param that differed from RN.');

request.description:
Flutter sent pageSize=20 until this session; RN sends 10 (APP_CONSTANT.PRODUCT_LIMIT). I already aligned the app to 10.

If this 500s and request 1 does not, page size was the cause and the fix is already in.

item.name: 6. Reference — product detail (proves the vendor slug)

exec: console.log('This is exactly the value both apps pass as shopUrl.');

request.description: The product from your run log. Confirms sold_by_vendor_url_key is where shopUrl comes from — RN productdetails/index.js:496-499, Flutter navigation_extensions.dart pushToBrandProduct.
